title: Domestic freedom beyond assumed attachment

captions.physics: Maintaining familiar comfort at freedom’s expense
captions.energy: Filling unknowns with anxious domestic accounts
captions.emotions: Feeling attachment to familiar material support

meaning: Your domestic support becomes freer when binding action and attachment are named directly instead of uncertainty preserving every familiar quantity beyond choice.
text: The Devil in the physical position of Muladhara describes actions maintaining familiar comfort even at the cost of free choice. The Moon in energy complicates them through anxious explanations of the unknown. The Devil in emotions feels attachment to material support. The repeated card distinguishes action from experience. Both retain the familiar because losing a possibility feels difficult. Another guess supposedly confirms it would be still harder for the other although actual attitudes remain unclear and may differ from this prepared domestic account.

For example, several identical dishes remain just in case. Releasing them worries both, but conversation is difficult because each imagines the other experiences reduction as insufficient provision. **Shared attachment neither reveals the other’s unknown feeling nor cancels choice.** You can name personal experience and objects’ actual use. Support returns to both without quantity receiving indefinite protection from two silent assumptions about what each supposedly must preserve for the other.

The difficulty is considering worry knowledge of actual need. Objects remain untouchable although conditions were never discussed. Separating usefulness, feeling and guess offers more dependable support: none replaces the rest. Home supports both through selecting enough according to accessible facts instead of every material habit automatically representing all shared care’s value and confidence about domestic tomorrow. Real clarity can reduce the weight of an imagined obligation.
